references.text: Moses sprinkled blood on the people as part of the covenant ceremony, a parallel to how the high priest sprinkles blood on the mercy seat.
Blood from the bull is used in the consecration of priests, just as it is used on the Day of Atonement.
The priest shall sprinkle the blood seven times before the LORD, before the veil of the sanctuary, following the same practice as at the mercy seat.
The priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD, identical to the ritual in Leviticus 16:14.
The same sprinkling ritual is performed with the goat's blood, which follows directly after the bull's blood.
The blood is sprinkled seven times on the altar to cleanse it, the same number of sprinklings as at the mercy seat.
The priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the tabernacle, a similar ritual.
Hebrews explains that the high priest entered the Most Holy Place once a year with blood for his own sins and those of the people.
Christ entered the sanctuary with his own blood, not with the blood of goats and calves, fulfilling the Day of Atonement ritual.
The high priest entered the sanctuary each year with blood that was not his own, referring to the practice of the Day of Atonement.
Blood from bulls and goats cannot take away sins, a theological comment on the ritual in Leviticus 16.
